name: あんかけスパゲティ NANAYA (Ankake Spaghetti NANAYA)

claims.text: The restaurant's core product is wheat spaghetti; the kitchen works exclusively with wheat pasta and there is no indication of any gluten-free preparation area or protocols.
Ankake spaghetti sauce may contain soy sauce, which in Japan standardly contains wheat. No source confirms NANAYA uses tamari or any gluten-free soy sauce alternative.
Noodles are fried in lard and standard toppings include wieners and egg; no plant-only preparation line exists.

name: あんかけ太郎 名古屋城金シャチ横丁店 (Ankake Taro Nagoya Castle Kinshachi Yokocho)

claims.text: The entire menu is wheat-pasta based and the kitchen is not set up to avoid gluten cross-contact. There is no gluten-free pasta, no GF sauce variant, and no allergen management information published.
The Japonaise menu style uses soy-dashi seasoning; standard Japanese soy sauce contains wheat. No wheat-free soy sauce alternative is mentioned.
All cooking stations handle lard-coated noodles and animal-based stocks simultaneously; there is no separation for plant-based preparation.
No allergen chart or staff allergy-handling protocol is published on the official site or any listing reviewed. Callers may reach the restaurant at 052-212-5554 to ask directly.
グルテンフリー専用の調理環境・フライヤーについての情報はなし。コースにパスタ（タリアテッレ等）が含まれるため厨房での小麦粉の使用は常態的と考えられる。セリアック病レベルの対応確認は予約時に直接必要。
メニューに醤油の記載なし。イタリアン主体の調理のため醤油・味噌の使用は限定的と推測されるが、和食材（ハモ、和牛、ウニ等）使用時の調味料については確認が必要。
バター・チーズ・生クリームが標準的に使用されるイタリアンコース構成。動物性食材の排除については予約時のリクエストが必要。
予約時にアレルギーや苦手な食材をコメント欄で伝えるよう案内されており、スタッフは対応を検討してくれる姿勢がある（「おいしく食べていただけるように工夫します」）。ただし書面によるアレルゲン対応保証の情報はない。
契約農家からの無農薬野菜を多用しており、野菜の質と鮮度へのこだわりは高い。コース内に豊富な野菜料理が含まれる。

No specific cross-contamination controls for gluten have been confirmed. The kitchen prepares a multi-course French tasting menu that routinely includes pastry and bread; shared preparation surfaces are expected.
No soy sauce used in a French kitchen context, but wheat appears in standard French sauces, roux, pastry, and bread service inherent to this omakase format.
The kitchen is not vegan-dedicated. Butter, cream, and other animal products are central to the French technique used throughout the omakase.

Allergy and dietary restriction information is collected from all members of the party at the reservation stage. The restaurant explicitly states that guests with wide-ranging allergies may not be able to be accommodated due to the fixed omakase format.
Pre-reservation allergy screening is conducted for every guest — the restaurant proactively requests allergy information before confirming the booking.

name: カフェ ド SaRa (Cafe de SaRa)

claims.text: Toast — wheat bread — is the core product of this cafe. Flour is present throughout the kitchen. No allergen controls or gluten-free procedures have been noted anywhere in available sources. This venue is not appropriate for anyone with celiac disease.
Dairy and eggs appear throughout the menu (butter on toast, egg toast, cream-based sweets). No vegan accommodation has been documented.
Entirely non-smoking interior.

name: Cafe & Bar REAL (Cafe&Bar REAL / カフェ&バー リアル)

claims.text: ashiya-obentofesta: 完全なグルテンフリー専門店であるかどうかは確認が取れていません — cannot confirm it is a complete GF specialist; contact directly for celiac/severe allergy.
Operates a live bar; barley beer/alcohol on the same premises is a cross-contact and dedicated-status concern.
十割 (100% buckwheat) mazesoba is offered, but its tare/sauce likely uses wheat-containing soy sauce unless tamari — unstated; ask.
Pork patties and dairy on-site; not a vegan kitchen.
No published allergen/cross-contact protocol; JP guide advises confirming directly for celiac.
Owner personally follows a gluten-free diet after illness; in-house rice-flour buns, pizza, cheesecake, scones; soy-milk/non-caffeine drinks.

name: カフェ キャメッロ (Caffe CAMMELLO)

claims.text: House-baked wheat bread (focaccia, ciabatta) is the core product; flour is actively used throughout the kitchen. Cross-contamination risk for gluten is high and no GF protocols are documented.
Butter, dairy, and eggs appear throughout the baked-goods and sandwich menu; no vegan-safe preparation areas noted.

name: 馳走菴 ひじり (Chisoan Hijiri)

claims.text: No information available on cross-contamination controls; the kitchen prepares wheat-battered tempura and standard soy-sauce-based dishes.

Wheat-based soy sauce is standard throughout Kyoto kaiseki cooking and appears inherent to the braises, simmered dishes, and seasoning at this restaurant; no tamari or gluten-free soy sauce alternative is noted anywhere.

Dashi made from katsuobushi (bonito flakes) is the backbone of Kyoto kaiseki; fish and poultry are central to the menu, making vegan cross-contact virtually certain without specific advance arrangement.

No allergen menu, allergy-handling policy, or gluten-free accommodation is mentioned on the official site or any reviewed source; the restaurant takes reservations by phone (052-963-0073) and dietary needs should be communicated at the time of booking.
Courses are prepared to order in small batches at a 7-seat counter, giving the chef direct visibility over every dish and some flexibility to accommodate requests if communicated well in advance.
